features.description: Extend Config with an optional defaultDestination and make token optional. Add a merge writer (read-modify-write that preserves both token and destination, re-asserting mode 0600) and make readConfig tolerant of legacy files (no defaultDestination) and destination-only files (no token).
preconditions: src/config.ts exists with Config { token; username; source } and writeConfig that overwrites the whole object at mode 0600
expectedBehavior: Config interface gains `defaultDestination?: { owner; repo }` and `token`/`username`/`source` become optional to support destination-only files
A merge writer persists a destination without dropping a saved token, and a token without dropping a saved destination
readConfig returns a usable Config for legacy files (no defaultDestination) and for destination-only files (no token), never null/throw for those shapes
Every write path (token save and destination save) re-asserts file mode 0600
Existing token-resolution guard on a present, non-empty token still holds (missing token = no saved token)

features.description: A pure-ish destination resolver mirroring auth.ts resolveTokenSource(resolvers): injected getters for parsed flags, config defaultDestination, an Octokit-backed verifyDestination (single repos.get reading permissions.push), and an interactive prompt. Returns a typed destination or throws typed bad-args (exit 1) / API-error (exit 2) outcomes. Owns precedence, verification, the §6.1 write-permission message, and the INV-READONLY guarantee. Adds the github.ts verifyDestination wrapper (takes an octokit, never a raw token).
preconditions: config-destination is complete (defaultDestination readable from config)
expectedBehavior: Precedence: flags (with --primary/--sandbox mutually exclusive, rejected before either is honored) → interactive(TTY) → saved-default(non-TTY) → bad-args error
--primary → destination = source, no prompt; --sandbox owner/repo (existing+writable) → that repo, no prompt; --sandbox == source → destination=source, sandbox flag false
Non-interactive with no flag: saved default used if present (after verify), else bad-args (exit 1) naming --primary/--sandbox

Verification is a single repos.get reading permissions.push, run after resolution and before any clone/push/create; 404 and not-writable handled with re-prompt (interactive) / exit 2 (non-interactive), never falling back to another repo
§6.1 write-permission message names the repo + missing capability, and names a known-writable saved sandbox when the failing destination is the primary
When destination != source, the source owner/repo is never an argument to any write/create call (recorded-call assertion)

features.description: Octokit sandbox creation wrapper: private always, owner defaulting to the source PR owner, routing personal-account → repos.createForAuthenticatedUser and org → repos.createInOrg. Wires into the resolver's create path (interactive create choice and --sandbox X --create-sandbox for a missing X). 403 never falls through to a source write. Preserves token safety on the create path (wrapper takes an octokit, never a raw token).
preconditions: destination-resolve is complete (the resolver exposes an injected createSandbox getter and a create path)
github.ts pattern for Octokit wrappers exists
expectedBehavior: Creation sets the repo private (never more visible) and defaults owner to the source owner; chooses createForAuthenticatedUser vs createInOrg by owner type
Creation 403 never writes the source repo; interactive re-prompts (create/different/primary), non-interactive exits 2 with a message naming the owner + missing permission
--sandbox X --create-sandbox creates a missing X and uses it; --sandbox X alone with X missing exits 2 without creating or writing anything else
Token never appears in a URL, on a git command line, or in any log on the create/verify paths
verificationSteps: Manual: --sandbox <throwaway-private> --create-sandbox -y against a real repo, confirm the backtest PR opens (VAL-CREATE-003)

features.description: The prompts-based destination selection menu and its sub-flows: the saved-default menu {primary, saved-sandbox, different}, the no-default menu {primary, create, different}, the 'A different repo…' slug prompt + verify, and the single 'remember as default?' prompt that persists via the config merge writer.
preconditions: destination-resolve is complete and accepts an injected prompt getter
sandbox-create create path exists (for the 'create a sandbox' choice)
expectedBehavior: Saved-default + TTY: choice set is {primary, saved-sandbox, different}; no create row
No-default + TTY: choice set is {primary, create, different}; no saved row
'A different repo…' prompts for owner/repo (parseRepoSlug), verifies it, and offers to save it
Resolving any non-primary, non-default destination triggers one remember-as-default prompt; yes persists via the merge writer
verificationSteps: Manual: run against a PR URL with and without a saved default, confirm menu rows (VAL-INT-001/002)

features.description: Replace --fork with --primary / --sandbox <owner/repo> / --create-sandbox in src/cli.ts; wire the destination resolver into runBacktest in src/index.ts (resolve destination before the clone, route findExistingPr/createPullRequest/pushBranchFromSha to the destination, keep source reads on the source); enforce exit-code mapping (--primary+--sandbox → exit 1; verification/creation failures → exit 2). Add test/cli.test.ts (subprocess harness for numeric exit codes and --help). No new dependency.
expectedBehavior: --fork is removed everywhere in src/; --primary/--sandbox/--create-sandbox are registered commander options visible in --help
--primary and --sandbox together exits 1 without any write; resolver is wired so verification runs before cloneRepo
--create-sandbox without --sandbox is a no-op (documented), resolution proceeds as if absent
findExistingPr (pre-flight) and the 422-recovery lookup are called with the destination owner/repo when destination != source
package.json dependencies are unchanged
verificationSteps: grep -n 'fork' src/  # expect no --fork flag remaining

features.description: Update src/plan.ts to the §8 read/write split: tag the source `(read-only)` and show the destination as the distinct write target only when destination != source; show one repo plainly when destination == source. Migrate/remove test/plan.fork.test.ts. Update README to document the destination model, the read-only guarantee, the new flags, and the §6.2 two-repo token requirement; update src/auth.ts interactive token guidance for the two-repo scope. Final tsc/lint gate.
preconditions: cli-and-index is complete (PlanInput carries the destination; --fork wording is being removed)
expectedBehavior: destination != source → plan tags source `(read-only)` and shows destination as the write target, distinctly
destination == source → plan does NOT tag `(read-only)`; one repo shown as both read and write site
test/plan.fork.test.ts is migrated into test/plan.test.ts or removed (its --fork wording is gone)
README documents primary-vs-sandbox, the read-only guarantee, --primary/--sandbox/--create-sandbox, and the two-repo token note; auth.ts guidance states the two-repo requirement
npm run build is clean (also satisfies lint-clean: no separate linter configured)
verificationSteps: Manual: read README for the destination model + token note (VAL-GATE-003)
